key_insight: Post-selection and entanglement are distinct resources: post-selection can boost CHSH weak correlations, but only entanglement lets those correlations exceed the separable pre- and post-selected bounds.
engineering_relevance: The result suggests hybrid measurement protocols that use post-selection plus entanglement to strengthen quantum sensing, weak-value amplification, and entanglement detection.
method: Compare anomalous weak values of the CHSH operator in pre- and post-selected ensembles.
Optimize the weak value first for a fixed Bell operator, then over all CHSH operators.
Analyze three boundary-state cases: unrestricted, one separable boundary state, and both boundary states separable.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports derived maxima and separable bounds across the three PPS scenarios, and a constructive protocol that detects every pure two-qubit source state with nonzero concurrence in the ideal state-adapted setting.
watch_item: The strongest witness performance is shown in an idealized, state-adapted setup, so practical implementations may face calibration, post-selection loss, and noise sensitivity.
paper_title: Quantum nonlocal correlations of anomalous weak values
